Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on SLO and autoscaling requirements: 

1) High-level SLOs you called out:
   - 95th p95 response latency target for interactive flows: 200ms end-to-end (user-to-response)
   - Throughput: steady-state ~120 requests/sec, peak bursts up to 900 req/sec for short windows (~2–5 minutes)
   - Concurrent streams: up to ~180 concurrent streaming sessions during peak bursts

2) Important constraints / asks from FastPay:
   - Streaming support with per-token low-latency tail behavior (small incremental tokens)
   - Scale-up tolerance: acceptable cold-scale window is ~60s; prefer <30s for critical checkout flows
   - Warm pool preference: want a small warm pool for critical model variants to shave scale-up time

3) Data / artifacts we requested:
   - Traffic sample (RPS by minute) and 2 weeks of peak-day traces (you mentioned you can share)
   - Answers to the short SLO questionnaire (attached)

4) Next steps / owners:
   - FastPay: share traffic sample and quick answers to the attached SLO_questionnaire.pdf (Sarah) — target by Wed 6/30
   - Redwood: technical deep-dive with Vivek to go over warm pools/queueing behavior and quantify scale-up latency (Marissa to schedule)
   - Contracting/TS: Rishi will start sizing and a rough cost estimate once we have sample traffic

I've attached our autoscale capabilities doc and a short SLO questionnaire to make the follow-up easier. I'll set up a 30-min call with Vivek for Wednesday — propose 10:00am PT unless that doesn't work.

Thanks — talk soon.

Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed recap — this matches what we discussed. Quick answers while we pull the raw traces: 

- Latency: the 95th target of 200ms is what we want for the checkout UX. For background processing (batch enrichment) we can tolerate higher latency.
- Steady RPS: our normal day is ~120rps. We see predictable increases around payroll windows; recent peak day hit ~780rps for 3–4 minutes.
- Concurrent streaming: we currently have about 130 simultaneous streaming sessions at peak, but we're expecting that to grow to ~180 over Q3.
- Queueing policy: we prefer soft-queueing—reject above hard limit rather than piling up long queues that block checkout.
- Warm pools: yes, would prefer a small warm pool for the checkout model (2–4 warm instances) to improve tail latencies.

I've attached a small CSV (fastpay-traffic-sample.csv) with a 24-hour minute-level sample and a one-page notes doc. We'll try to get 2 weeks of traces but can start with the 24-hour sample.

Also, Wed 6/30 at 10:00am PT works for a short call with Vivek.

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks for the sample and the quick answers. A few technical notes ahead of our call so we can use the time to converge on numbers: 

1) Warm pools:
   - Recommendation: maintain a warm pool of lightweight warm containers (model runner processes with loaded weights, KV cache empty) sized to handle ~15–25% of expected peak concurrency for the critical checkout model. For your expected 180 concurrent streams, a 25% warm pool => ~45 warm instances.
   - Warm instance cost/benefit: a warm instance reduces cold-start token latency from ~6–10s to sub-300ms for first tokens in many cases (depending on model).

2) Scale-up/backfill strategy:
   - Continuous autoscaler: we recommend a hybrid policy — aggressive scale-up based on sustained CPU/GPU utilization + short-term burst policy triggered by queue depth/spike detection.
   - Scale-up time target: we can confidently hit ~20–35s to bring additional GPU-backed runners online if warm pools are used; cold provisioning without warm pools can be 60–90s depending on hardware and region.

3) Queueing behavior and SLO enforcement:
   - Soft-queueing window: allow a short buffer (<=10s) for transient bursts; apply priority-based shedding for low-value background requests to protect checkout paths.
   - Hard limits: configure hard rejection at ~x1.5 of provisioned concurrency to avoid unbounded queue growth.

4) Streaming:
   - For token-level streaming, prioritize small-batch, low-latency kernels; ensure KV cache priming on warm instances to reduce tail.

5) Data/metrics we need for exact sizing:
   - Per-minute arrival histogram (you provided a good sample — 24h ok to start)
   - Typical token counts for the streaming sessions, and average session duration

I'll bring example configs and a rough cost delta (warm pool vs no warm pool) to the call. If you want numbers up front I can run a quick sizing with your CSV and share before the meeting.

Best,
